newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet Q4 loss seen mounting -analysts.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet Q4 loss seen mounting -analysts.

text.p: Valujet Inc, its December holiday service marred by bureaucratic inaction, may be heading for a worse-than-expected fourth-quarter loss, analysts say.

The discount airline was expected to release December traffic data next Tuesday. Although analysts expect ValuJet's load factor to exceed a weak November reading of 48.2, the carrier's traffic levels were expected to remain well below that of the industry at large.
Analysts said the expected weakness would stem partly from the Federal Aviation Administration's decision not to allow ValuJet to add three new routes to its system for the holiday travel season.

But some believe the airline also has had some trouble attracting passengers in general, following its voluntary grounding in the aftermath of last May's Florida Everglades crash, which killed 110 people.
"The traffic rebuild is not ramping up as well as we had hoped and the political environment also remains muddied," said PaineWebber's Samuel Buttrick.
"As a result, clearly ValuJet's fourth-quarter losses will be larger than expected and the losses will continue well into 1997," he said.

Buttrick believes ValuJet could post a quarterly loss of about $18 million, or $0.30 per share. Until recently, the Street had been looking for a loss of $0.23 per share, according to the Institutional Brokers Estimate System. The company was expected to report fourth-quarter results by the first week in February.
Airline management has said the FAA-recertified operation would not reach the breakeven point until the number of aircraft in its fleet reached 30 from a current 15.

"My original estimate was they'd get back to that point about the middle of March, so that the June quarter of next year would be the first they'd break even and maybe make a little money. At this point, not knowing the politics at the FAA, I can't tell you what's happening," Pincavage said.
Meanwhile, a larger loss was not expected to have much effect on the ValuJet share price, which stood at 6-3/4 on the Nasdaq market on Thursday.
"The stock has lost more than half its value from the time ValuJet was recertified," said PaineWebber's Buttrick.
"The weakness has accelerated in the past two weeks, but I would associate that more with tax-loss selling than the most recent FAA hold-up."
